propositions: Agent-authored mutation scripts invoked by TDD skills (rebar-debug, rebar-implement) execute arbitrary code without OS sandbox isolation, creating risk of filesystem destruction as demonstrated by 2026-08-26 `rm -rf /*` incident.
Current CI mutation gate (e668) does not cover the defect-seeded mutation check path that skills instruct agents to perform during routine TDD, leaving the exposure present on every operator run.
Both rebar-debug (Step 5) and rebar-implement (4e) skills lack any mention of sandboxing mechanisms (sandbox-exec, bwrap) and must be updated to require OS-level write restrictions.

Mutation runs must execute within a sandbox denying writes outside the worktree and scratch directory; if no sandbox is available, the mutation step must fall back to asserting on an injected seam rather than proceeding unsandboxed.

The sandbox requirement must be self-contained inline in skill text with complete platform-specific invocations (macOS profile heredoc, Linux bwrap flags) and capability probes, rather than depending on external wrapper scripts.
